active_paradigms.description: The current hierarchy first assigns contiguous logical-expert groups to nodes using only each group's total token count, then replicates inside each node. This is strong because LPT equalizes raw node totals cheaply, but it ignores that a group containing one dominant expert benefits far more from the node's replica slots than a diffuse group with the same sum. Replace the group packing key with a replica-aware scalar computed directly from the group's sorted expert loads using torch.sort: estimate its post-replication bottleneck under the average physical-expert budget available per node. Pack groups in descending estimated bottleneck rather than descending group sum, while still using the existing cardinality-constrained heap assignment and preserving contiguous group structure. A practical estimate is the smallest threshold T for which sum over experts of ceil(load/T), clipped to the per-node physical capacity, predicts whether the group consumes disproportionate replica capacity; approximate this from the sorted prefix rather than solving an optimization problem. This changes the node decision to account for the downstream replication stage, which is the largest structural omission in the current program. Keep the existing global-policy fallback unchanged when hierarchy is disabled.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce the eventual maximum per-GPU expert load by preventing highly skewed groups from being co-located merely because their total loads appear balanced; preserve low runtime with a per-group sort already small relative to later processing.
active_paradigms.cautions: The adapter only exposes combined_score, not the original evaluator's metric breakdown, so validate this against both score and evaluator runtime rather than assuming sum-load balance is sufficient. Do not change group membership or violate equal groups-per-node capacity. Use float32/CPU consistently because the current function explicitly moves weights to CPU. The predictor must account for the fixed number of physical slots per node; otherwise it will overvalue replication that cannot actually be allocated.

active_paradigms.description: Current balanced_packing performs LPT and examines exactly one swap between the single most-loaded and single least-loaded pack. That is extremely fast and explains its robustness, but it misses the common case where the final maximum is improved by exchanging with the second or third lightest/heaviest pack, or where the old minimum ceases to matter after a swap. After LPT, use heapq.nlargest to identify a tiny critical set of highest-load packs and lowest-load packs, for example two or three from each side, and evaluate all legal one-for-one swaps among only those packs. Select the swap with the best lexicographic sorted load vector: first minimize maximum pack load, then minimize the second maximum, then range. Apply only a strictly improving swap and repeat for a fixed very small number of passes, such as two, terminating early if no improvement exists. This is a local-search refinement rather than the previously failed assignment, MILP, or flow formulations: it preserves the actual equal-slot packing constraints and directly optimizes the load vector produced by the placement. It should be applied independently to both group-to-node packing and replica-to-GPU packing, where the latter is particularly sensitive to a single overloaded GPU.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly lower bottleneck node/GPU load and tail imbalance after LPT while retaining predictable bounded overhead, which should improve the balance component without materially harming runtime.
active_paradigms.cautions: Compare the complete sorted vector or at least max then second-max, not only high-minus-low range: a swap can reduce range yet increase the maximum that likely drives service imbalance. Recompute loads for every candidate exactly and preserve per-pack cardinality and rank bookkeeping when accepted. Keep the critical set and pass count constant and small; exhaustive pack-pair local search can erase the current program's efficiency advantage. Avoid ties that churn placements without objective improvement.

active_paradigms.idea: Batched water-filling replica allocation with torch.searchsorted
active_paradigms.description: The current replicate_experts adds one replica at a time by repeatedly selecting argmax(weight/logcnt), which is the correct greedy water-filling principle for minimizing the largest isolated replica share, but it performs one full reduction per redundant physical expert and does not expose a direct threshold representation. For each layer/node, use torch.searchsorted over sorted candidate breakpoints load/k for k from 1 through the maximum possible replica count to find a common water level whose required replica counts sum to the physical-expert budget. Set each expert's replica count to ceil(load/level), clamped to at least one, then use a deterministic correction for any residual slots based on the next marginal load reduction. This produces the same or near-identical minimax allocation as sequential greedy but in a batched form, and makes it affordable to use the replica-aware group score proposed above. Because all replicas of an expert have equal load under the evaluator's presumed split model, this also gives a clean predicted physical load vector for the subsequent GPU LPT phase. Retain the existing rank construction after counts are decided, so the output maps and scatter-based inverse mapping remain valid. This targets efficiency first, but the exact threshold calculation can also remove float tie-order artifacts from repeated argmax decisions across layers.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce rebalance execution time in replication-heavy configurations and stabilize or improve the maximum per-replica load that feeds GPU packing, improving the combined score if evaluator runtime is included.
active_paradigms.cautions: The original evaluator is not shown beyond its process wrapper, so first verify whether its combined score rewards runtime, balance, or both; do not trade a measurable balance loss for speed blindly. Handle zero-load experts, equality at breakpoints, and integer residual-slot correction deterministically so counts sum exactly to num_phy. Breakpoints must include all feasible k values up to the available redundant-slot budget, not merely a fixed small k, or highly hot experts will be under-replicated. This replaces only count selection; placement must still honor node boundaries and physical expert rank indexing.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace LPT packing with an exact cardinality-constrained minimax MILP for the small per-layer packing subproblems
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first applies LPT to assign fixed-size groups to nodes and physical replicas to GPUs, then considers only one swap between the globally lightest and heaviest packs. This is fast, but it can leave large improvements requiring a coordinated cycle of several moves or a swap involving non-extreme packs. Formulate each call to `balanced_packing` as a minimax binary assignment model solved by `scipy.optimize.milp`: binary variable x[i,p] means item i is assigned to pack p, every item is assigned once, every pack receives exactly `groups_per_pack` items, and each pack load is constrained to be at most a scalar makespan T. Minimize T directly, using integrality=1 and sparse `LinearConstraint` matrices. Use this only below a conservative size threshold, such as at most 32 items or a modest variable budget; retain the present LPT implementation for larger instances. The model is especially attractive for the group-to-node stage because group counts are usually much smaller than the number of replicas and this stage determines the topology-locality ceiling for all later decisions. For the GPU stage, solve the MILP only when there are few GPUs per node, where exact packing can materially improve the worst GPU load at negligible total evaluator cost. Reconstruct `pack_index` from selected variables and assign `rank_in_pack` deterministically by sorted original item index, preserving all map-shape and rank invariants.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce maximum node and GPU load directly rather than merely reducing the range of the current LPT solution; this targets the likely dominant load-balance component of the scalar score while retaining a fast fallback for runtime-sensitive large cases.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The shown adapter exposes only `combined_score`, not the original evaluator's component formula, so validate MILP thresholds against the real evaluator rather than assuming exact optimization always wins after solver overhead. Set a strict per-instance `time_limit`, accept only solver solutions with a valid integral assignment, and fall back to LPT on timeout or non-success. Do not formulate all layers jointly: layers are independent in the current output contract, and a joint model would be unnecessarily expensive. Keep all tensors CPU/int64 and ensure exactly one rank is emitted for every slot in each pack.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use a slot-expanded linear assignment to globally repair GPU placement after replication
tried_paradigms.description: The current second packing stage treats every replica as an independent item and LPT assigns it greedily to GPU packs with a one-pair swap. Instead, create one column per physical GPU slot and solve `scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment` over replicas versus slots. Construct the cost matrix from the load of each replica and a target per-GPU load: assigning a heavier replica to a slot belonging to a currently under-target GPU receives lower cost, while assignment to an over-target GPU receives a convex overload penalty. Include deterministic tiny tie-break terms based on GPU and original physical index so mappings are stable. Each GPU has exactly `phy_experts_per_gpu` duplicated slot columns, therefore the assignment automatically preserves the hard equal-expert-count constraint without any custom repair. This is a fundamentally broader move than the present extreme swap: one assignment call can permute every physical expert among all GPU slots simultaneously. Apply it independently within each node in hierarchical mode, so no replica crosses the node selected by the first-stage group packing. For global mode it naturally operates over all GPUs. Decode the assigned column into GPU index and rank, then use the existing inverse-permutation and logical-map reconstruction unchanged.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve the final per-GPU imbalance and remove local minima caused by LPT plus a single extreme-pair swap, while preserving the exact number of physical experts per GPU and topology constraints.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Linear assignment minimizes separable assignment costs, whereas true GPU load imbalance is coupled; the target and convex cost must be chosen from the replica-load total, not from the original logical loads. A dense replica-by-slot matrix can be too large, so use this only when `num_physical_experts` is moderate and retain current packing otherwise. The cost must not accidentally reward putting several heavy replicas onto the same GPU merely because its duplicated columns have identical costs; encode a distinct marginal overload cost for the first, second, and later slot of a GPU. Do not change `phyrank`: it remains the replica rank associated with the logical expert, independent of its assigned GPU slot.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use min-cost flow with marginal GPU-load arcs to make replication placement topology-aware
tried_paradigms.description: The key structural weakness is that replication and placement are optimized separately: `replicate_experts` greedily minimizes individual replica load within a node, then packing tries to place the resulting fixed replicas. Replace the placement decision with a discretized convex transportation model solved in one `networkx.network_simplex` call per layer/node. Create a source-to-expert supply arc for every required physical copy, expert-to-GPU arcs for legal GPUs in that node, and GPU-to-sink arcs representing expert slots. Give successive GPU capacity arcs increasing marginal costs based on projected load, so the min-cost-flow objective approximates squared load or a sharp penalty above average load. Expert-to-GPU arcs can additionally carry a locality-aware cost: zero within the group-selected node and prohibitively large or absent across nodes. Supply one unit for each physical replica slot, making both replica counts and GPU capacity exact integer constraints in the flow model. Decode the units leaving each expert into the needed `phy2log` entries and assign replica ranks consecutively, then build `logcnt` and `log2phy` exactly as in the current implementation. This permits the flow objective to decide where the extra copies of a hot expert are useful rather than committing all copy choices before seeing GPU capacities. It is particularly promising when a few very hot experts interact with uneven group/node totals, where independent greedy replication commonly over-concentrates the wrong logical experts within a node.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Jointly reduce GPU overload and replica-induced hotspots under exact node locality and fixed physical-slot constraints; this addresses the coupling that the current greedy replication plus LPT decomposition cannot see.
tried_paradigms.cautions: `networkx.network_simplex` requires integral demands, capacities, and costs, so scale floating loads to bounded integers carefully and use deterministic rounding; overflow or excessively large scales can make it slow. The convex load objective is an approximation through marginal-cost arcs, so choose a small number of load quanta and fall back to the current method if the graph would be large. Preserve the required total number of replicas and never allow an expert to receive zero copies. If the evaluator expects the hierarchical group-to-node policy, restrict arcs to the selected node rather than allowing globally cheaper cross-node placement.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace the final physical-expert-to-GPU LPT packing with a per-layer minimax mixed-integer linear program using scipy.optimize.milp
tried_paradigms.description: The current program first greedily chooses replica counts, then uses cardinality-constrained LPT twice: groups to nodes and physical replicas to GPUs. Its strongest feature is that it reduces each decision to independent per-row packing, so it is fast and produces valid exact-capacity placements. Its principal weakness is that LPT plus one swap is only a local heuristic: the one allowed swap considers only the currently lightest and heaviest pack, cannot make a coordinated cycle of moves, and can miss substantially better assignments. Keep the existing group-to-node and replica-count construction, but replace Step 3 with one scipy.optimize.milp call independently for each layer/node. Create binary variables x[p,g] for assigning each already-created physical replica p to each local GPU g, enforce one GPU per replica and exactly phy_experts_per_gpu replicas per GPU, and add a continuous makespan variable z with sum_p replica_load[p]*x[p,g] <= z for every GPU. Minimize z, using scipy.optimize.Bounds and scipy.optimize.LinearConstraint, and recover the permutation/rank tensors from the binary solution. This directly optimizes the bottleneck that LPT is attempting to approximate while preserving the current output contract and hierarchical node locality.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Primary balance quality: minimize the maximum per-GPU replica load after replication, especially adversarial rows where a single swap cannot repair LPT. Use it only when the local replica count is small enough that solve time remains below the evaluator timeout.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The provided wrapper does not expose the original evaluator's combined-score formula, so validate whether it scores maximum load, imbalance range, and runtime before committing. Solve independently per layer and node; a global MILP is unnecessarily large. Set integrality=1 only on assignment variables, give z a nonnegative continuous bound, use a finite time_limit if supported, and fall back to the present LPT result if the solver returns no feasible incumbent. Do not alter phy2log/phyrank semantics: only reorder existing physical replicas, then rebuild inverse permutations exactly as the current code does.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use networkx.min_cost_flow for a convex-cost replica-placement formulation rather than greedy heap packing
tried_paradigms.description: Model each local packing stage as a single min-cost-flow graph whose flow units are physical replica items and whose sink-side parallel arcs represent progressively more expensive capacity on each GPU. The current LPT method greedily commits a large replica before seeing which later replicas must fill the remaining fixed slots; its one extreme swap repairs only one pair and therefore does not capture coordinated reassignment. Construct a source-to-replica arc of capacity one, replica-to-GPU-slot arcs of capacity one, and GPU-slot-to-sink arcs whose increasing marginal costs encode the desired load-balancing penalty around the target local average. Set the replica-to-slot costs from each replica's post-replication load times that slot's marginal penalty, then call networkx.min_cost_flow once. The resulting integral flow supplies a valid exact-cardinality GPU assignment without a custom heap or local-search loop. This is particularly attractive if the evaluator rewards broad distribution rather than only the single maximum, because convex slot costs discourage concentration across all GPUs. Use the existing hierarchy and greedy replication allocation initially, so the graph only replaces the final physical placement decision.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Reduce global per-GPU load spread and tail imbalance with a polynomial-time integral optimization, while avoiding the potentially variable runtime of a full MILP.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Min-cost flow has a linear arc-cost objective, not an exact max-load objective; choose marginal slot penalties to approximate the evaluator's imbalance metric and compare against LPT on representative workload rows. Costs should be scaled to integers because NetworkX flow implementations are most reliable with integer demands/costs; preserve ordering deterministically for ties. The graph can grow as replicas times GPUs times slots, so apply it per layer/node and retain LPT for unusually large instances. Exact fixed replica counts must be enforced by the number of GPU-slot arcs, not merely by soft costs.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment as an exact assignment solver for targeted group-to-node repair around the current hierarchical layout
tried_paradigms.description: The hierarchy currently packs groups by their total load before it knows how much replication will later be needed inside each node. Consequently, a node can receive a mix whose aggregate group total looks balanced but whose concentrated hot experts consume many local replica slots and leave a worse achievable GPU makespan. Retain the current group ordering as a baseline, compute a per-group pressure score such as its predicted local bottleneck after the deterministic replica rule, and build a square cost matrix between group positions and node-specific group slots. The cost for placing group q into a node slot should include its pressure plus a deterministic penalty for moving it away from its original node, thereby allowing only beneficial cross-node changes. Call scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment once per layer to obtain a globally consistent reassignment of groups to node slots, then run the unchanged replication and local GPU packer. This differs from changing the GPU packer: it improves the upstream partition that determines which experts are even allowed to share replica capacity. It can be much faster than MILP because assignment is cubic in group count and has predictable runtime.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Improve hierarchical balance by reducing node-level hot-expert concentration before replica allocation; preserve or improve execution time relative to multi-swap local search or MILP.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Linear assignment optimizes additive placement costs, so the pressure score must be derived carefully from the actual replica-allocation bottleneck rather than raw group token sum alone. The current code requires each node to receive exactly groups_per_node contiguous logical-group slots; preserve this cardinality and reconstruct log2mlog/mlog2log consistently. If the evaluator penalizes movement or requires stable mappings across invocations, increase the movement penalty and deterministic tie breaking. Because the actual evaluator formula is absent from the shown wrapper, benchmark raw-load pressure, max-expert pressure, and predicted replica-load pressure rather than assuming one is correct.
